newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Veltroni hails market reaction to budget.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Veltroni hails market reaction to budget.

text.p: Italian Deputy Prime Minister Walter Veltroni on Thursday said financial markets supported the government's plan to significantly cut the deficit in next year's budget.

He was referring to markets' enthusiastic reaction after the government revealed that the 1997 budget would include cuts aimed at slashing the deficit by 50 trillion lire ($32.9 billion) and bring the country in line to meet requirements to join a single European currency.
After the announcement on Thursday, the lira rose to 994.4 against the mark, its highest level in more than two years, while bond prices surged to new record highs.

"The reaction of the markets is an excellent demonstration of the priorities that they (the markets) value: stable government and the possibility that Italy will enter Europe (single currency)," Veltroni said. "The work that we are finishing up is inspired by these objectives.
The budget, which was originally expected to seek savings of 32.4 trillion lire next year, will be formally unveiled on Friday.
